What this version supports
Write DATA steps against datasets in the WORK library. Dataset and variable names are case-insensitive. Every statement ends with a semicolon.
Programs and project folders
Open and save .sas programs. Choose a project folder in Chrome or Edge to enable programmatic CSV access. The app remembers the folder handle in this browser when supported; use Reconnect folder if permission expires. Browser permissions and remembered folders are not transferred when moving the app to another computer or browser.
File paths are relative to the chosen folder. Existing subfolders are supported. Absolute paths, URLs, parent traversal, and filesystem-wide access are unavailable. FILENAME aliases and CSV PROC IMPORT/EXPORT are supported; these file operations belong to the browser workflow. Other engines or offline test harnesses require an explicit file adapter.
filename source 'inputs/claims.csv';
proc import datafile=source out=claims dbms=csv replace;
  getnames=yes;
  guessingrows=max;
run;
data flagged;
  set claims;
  if paid_amount > 1000;
run;
proc export data=flagged outfile='outputs/flagged.csv' dbms=csv replace;
run;
Select a folder before Run. All exports are prepared until the program succeeds; each disk file is then saved. Existing targets require REPLACE. Multiple file saves cannot be atomic: failures may leave earlier exports saved, and the Log lists paths possibly changed. Dataset changes are committed only when exports succeed. Imports read disk files or a prior prepared export at the identical relative path in the same run. CSV files are limited to 20 MB each, with 50 MB of exports per program. Save Program and manual Save CSV are explicit save actions and can overwrite the chosen target.
Browsers without folder access still support program uploads, program downloads, and manual CSV import/download. Remembered editor text is a recovery draft, not a saved .sas file.
Permanent JSON libraries
Assign a library to an existing folder inside your selected project, or use '.' for the project root. One-level names use temporary WORK. Named tables are saved as .sassy-table.json files with versioned column descriptors and row objects. Bindings last for this session; files remain on disk. Reissue LIBNAME after reopening the app. These are not SAS7BDAT files.
libname saved 'tables';
data saved.reviewed;
  set work.claims;
  if paid_amount > 1000;
run;
/* Later, including in another run: */
data restored;
  set saved.reviewed;
run;
DATA and PROC SORT replace their named-library targets after successful computation. PROC IMPORT into a permanent library requires REPLACE. File reads/writes remain scoped to the selected project and never prompt during a run. Library files must be valid version-1 Sassy tables (20 MB, 100,000 rows, 1–1024 columns). Library writes share the 50 MB program-save limit. Multi-file saves are not atomic. LIBNAME name CLEAR removes the binding without deleting files. A library cannot be cleared or reassigned after writing to it in the same program. Refresh libraries updates the left-hand listing; clicking a saved member reads it. CSV import/export remains available for SAS interchange.
Charts — Chart.js
PROC SGPLOT supports one SCATTER, HBAR, VBAR or HISTOGRAM statement per procedure. PROC SGPIE supports PIE. DATA= is required and can name a WORK or assigned-library table. Charts append to session Output; choose one in its history dropdown and use Download PNG. Clear output removes charts and table snapshots, retaining WORK. Chart.js is embedded and works offline.
title 'Payments by provider';
proc sgplot data=claims;
  scatter x=allowed_amount y=paid_amount / group=provider;
  xaxis label='Allowed amount';
  yaxis label='Paid amount';
run;
proc sgplot data=claims;
  hbar provider / response=paid_amount stat=sum;
run;
proc sgplot data=claims;
  vbar provider / response=paid_amount stat=mean;
run;
proc sgplot data=claims;
  histogram paid_amount / nbins=10 scale=count;
run;
proc sgpie data=claims;
  pie provider / response=paid_amount stat=sum;
run;
title;
Bars and pie support STAT=FREQ/SUM/MEAN; default FREQ without RESPONSE and SUM with RESPONSE. Bars also support GROUP= and GROUPDISPLAY=STACK/CLUSTER (default STACK). Histograms support NBINS=1–100 and SCALE=COUNT/PERCENT/PROPORTION (default PERCENT); automatic binning uses bounded Sturges bins, not SAS's exact default algorithm. Numeric scatter/histogram values and responses must be numeric; missing/nonfinite observations are omitted with counts in the log. Missing categories/groups are omitted. Pie slices must be nonnegative with a positive total. Limits: 20 charts and 100,000 plotted values per run, 20,000 points per scatter, 200 categories and 50 groups. TITLE 'text'; and TITLE; persist/reset the session chart title. XAXIS/YAXIS support LABEL='text' only; titles/labels are limited to 200 characters. Overlays, regression, density curves, style attributes, PROC PLOT and other options are unsupported. Charts use raw values and first-seen category order; statistical and visual SAS equivalence has not been certified.
Statements
DATA, one SET per step, assignments, subsetting IF, IF / THEN / ELSE, DO / END, indexed DO i = 1 TO 10 BY 2, DELETE, STOP, OUTPUT (including named outputs), KEEP, DROP, RETAIN, sum statements (total + amount;), character LENGTH, and basic FORMAT.
BY groups
BY supports already-sorted data, including multiple keys and per-variable DESCENDING. Use FIRST.variable and LAST.variable. Unsorted input produces an error. PROC SORT can prepare it.
DATA step functions (35)
These are the 35 functions implemented in this app, not a complete SAS catalog. Names are case-insensitive. Brackets mean optional arguments, and … means repeated explicit arguments; OF variable lists and arrays are not supported. String handling, argument validation, type conversion, missing values, rounding, and date edge cases are a practical subset, not certified SAS behavior.

Conversion and random functions
FunctionBehavior


INPUT(text, informat.)Read text using a supported numeric, date/time, or character informat. Optional ? suppresses invalid-input notes; ?? also prevents setting _ERROR_. Width limits the text read.


PUT(value, format.)Return formatted text, with padding to the width. Optional -L, -C, or -R selects alignment. Format type must match the source.


RAND('UNIFORM' [, a [, b]])
RAND('NORMAL' [, mean [, sigma]])		Use CALL STREAMINIT('MT32', positive_seed); first. MT2002 is an alias. First initialization wins within a DATA step. The MT19937 integer core is verified; uniform values match all 40,000 draws in the supplied SAS seed-12345 fixture. Other seeds and the polar normal sampler remain unverified against SAS sequences. Default MTHYBRID and other generators/distributions fail clearly.


Expressions
Arithmetic, comparisons (including EQ NE GT GE LT LE), AND OR NOT, IN (…), ||, missing numeric ., _N_, and dates such as '01JAN2026'd.
Common formats (20 families) & CSV
Table display omits alignment padding. PUT returns padded strings. Width changes zero filling, date representation, truncation, and overflow. Numeric overflow shows asterisks instead of SAS adaptive precision fallback. Decimal precision is limited to 0–15; numeric rounding follows JavaScript. Character widths count JavaScript UTF-16 units, not SAS bytes.

Supported informats for INPUT
w.d / Fw.d / BESTw., COMMAw.d / DOLLARw.d, PERCENTw.d, DATEw., MMDDYYw., DDMMYYw., YYMMDDw., TIMEw., DATETIMEw., E8601DA10., E8601DTw.d, $w., $CHARw., and $UPCASEw.. Decimal-free numeric input uses implied precision d. Date validation rejects impossible dates; two-digit years use a fixed 1926–2025 window. Dates use days and times/datetimes use seconds; computations use UTC. This subset does not support every SAS separator, informat modifier, or special missing value.
CSV export contains raw dataset values. Formats do not change those stored values; PUT creates a character value whose padding is included in export. CSV types are inferred and headers must be unique SAS variable names.
MERGE
MERGE claims(in=a) providers(in=b); BY provider; supports two or more sorted inputs, unmatched observations, and repeated keys. Repeated groups are paired one observation at a time, with values carried forward when an input group is exhausted. The row count is the largest group count, rather than a Cartesian product.
IN= indicators are available during the step and excluded from output. Copy one into a new variable to save it. Shared columns are overwritten in input order only when that input is actually read. Input KEEP=, DROP=, and RENAME=(old=new) can separate overlapping columns. Character/numeric conflicts fail clearly.
PROC MEANS
Unweighted descriptive statistics: N, NMISS, SUM, MEAN, MIN, MAX, RANGE, VAR, STD/STDDEV, STDERR, CSS, USS and CV. DATA= is required; VAR lists numeric variables (default eligible numeric columns). CLASS generates all total/subtotal combinations for saved OUTPUT, identified by _TYPE_ and _FREQ_. NWAY keeps only full combinations. Inactive character class values are blank and numeric values missing. MISSING includes missing CLASS values; otherwise those observations are excluded from all types. BY input must be sorted, with DESCENDING supported.
proc means data=claims n nmiss mean std var;
    class provider;
    var paid_amount;
    output out=summary n= mean= std= var= / autoname;
run;
Displayed reports show full combinations, with N Obs distinct from per-variable N. OUTPUT OUT= supports explicit names, optional statistic(variable) subsets and AUTONAME. OUTPUT without statistic requests writes five _STAT_ rows: N, MIN, MAX, MEAN, STD. VARDEF=DF (sample) or N (population), NOPRINT and MAXDEC=0–15 supported. Defaults are N MEAN STD MIN MAX. STDERR requires VARDEF=DF. Up to 8 CLASS variables and bounded groups/rows. WEIGHT, FREQ, quantiles, tests, TYPES/WAYS, CHARTYPE and advanced options are unsupported. SAS runtime comparisons are pending for the new procedure.
PROC SORT
PROC SORT DATA=claims OUT=sorted; BY provider DESCENDING paid_amount; RUN; sorts by one or more keys. Omit OUT= to replace the input. NODUPKEY keeps the first observation for each complete BY key. Equal keys retain their original order. Numeric missing values sort first in ascending order.
Macros
%LET, &variable and &variable., %MACRO / %MEND, positional and keyword parameters, %IF / %THEN / %ELSE, block or indexed %DO / %END with %TO / %BY, %LOCAL, %GLOBAL, %PUT, integer %EVAL, and %UPCASE. Macro variables resolve in double-quoted strings and remain literal in single-quoted strings.
Use Expanded code to inspect generated statements. Definitions and macro variables reset with each Run. This is a text-generation subset: no macro quoting functions, indirect && references, %SYSFUNC, runtime CALL SYMPUT, dynamic macro names, or full SAS rescanning. Conditions support simple text comparisons and integer expressions; empty operands and advanced macro expressions are unsupported.
Important limits
This is not the SAS runtime. Character variables without LENGTH use flexible strings; numeric/character type coercion, truncation rules, and function edge cases are not fully SAS-compatible. No positional MERGE without BY, arrays, other PROC procedures, INPUT/INFILE, INPUT/PUT statements, unlisted informats, output dataset options, variable lists, special missing values, or SAS7BDAT files. Unsupported syntax fails; unsupported semantic edge cases may still differ from SAS.
100,000 rows per dataset; execution and macro expansion are bounded. Character sort order uses Unicode, which can differ from SAS locale or host collation. Datasets and code are kept only in memory. Importing the same dataset name replaces it. Use test data until you have checked your programs against SAS.
